title: Associate restore snapshot task to parent mount task

timeline.body:
Implemented the test as an integration test that polls the tasks API to confirm the association of parent/child tasks. Thanks for the feedback @DaveCTurner.

Closes #105830
`setParentTask` doesn't follow the fluent pattern the other setters do, so this had to be separate

reply.body: You could use a `org.elasticsearch.client.internal.ParentTaskAssigningClient` if you really wanted a one-liner here.
I think it's probably overkill in this case, but thanks!

timeline.body: I had to use `UUID.randomUUID().toString()` here instead of `randomUUID()` because of a security context error. This is the first time I've used the `LuceneTestCase` methods so open to suggestions if this is wrong.

reply.body: Randomness isn't available in `static` context here, but there's no need for this constant to be `static`.
Ahh this is because of the reproducible randomness thing (being in the context of the seed). Makes sense!

timeline.body:
Yeah mocking this much stuff is pretty bad IMO, it will get in the way of future changes/refactorings to these APIs I'm sure.

I would suggest doing this as a `org.elasticsearch.xpack.searchablesnapshots.BaseSearchableSnapshotsIntegTestCase` which gives you real implementations of all this stuff. Submit a task to the master which blocks, something like this:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/69ff7dfb2010872381f2f45ffc96c83595fb5672/server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/routing/BatchedRerouteServiceTests.java#L89-L101

(get the `clusterService` using `internalCluster().getCurrentMasterNodeInstance(ClusterService.class)`)

That will give you time to call the list-tasks API and verify that the mount task is the parent of the restore task.
There's no point retrying here if this fails, I'll move that out of the `assertBusy` somehow. Perhaps `assertBusy` isn't appropriate here, I just wanted to avoid polling the list tasks API forever.
This still looks a bit janky, if there's a more suitable pattern about please advise. The idea was to just limit how long we poll the tasks API for, in the event something goes wrong.

reply.body: I think just sticking an `assertBusy` around the whole thing would be fine. We only wait 10s if something goes wrong. It's true that any other failures in here will also cause `assertBusy` to retry but that's not really the point of this test, we have other tests to check these things.

I went ahead with just using `assertBusy` for readability. To do this with the observer, I think we'd need to add the observer, submit the mount task, then wait on the observer which would mean it'd all need to be inline so probably not worth it given we're not too fussed about polling. Perhaps if there's value in it we could add something like `T ESTestCase#doSomethingThenWaitForIndexCreation(Supplier<T> action)` down the track.

timeline.message: Wait for mount to complete, delete index at end of test
timeline.author: Nick Tindall

timeline.body: The `actionGet` and delete index here were an attempt to fix [a failure that occurred in CI in a teardown](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/762xzz33sxoqg/tests/task/:x-pack:plugin:searchable-snapshots:internalClusterTest/details/org.elasticsearch.xpack.searchablesnapshots.SearchableSnapshotsIntegTests/testMountingSnapshotLinksRefreshTaskAsChild?expanded-stacktrace=WyIwLTEiXQ&top-execution=1), one or both of these may be necessary. Happy to remove the delete if it's not necessary.

reply.body:
Nice catch, yeah, it seems we have to wait for the mount to complete before finishing the test or else there's a race between cleaning up the test cluster and the mount process creating the internal `.snapshot-blob-cache` index.

I expect there's no need to manually delete the test index here tho but it doesn't hurt either. Would you add a code comment about why we need these nonobvious cleanup steps?

timeline.body: If we run this whole thing in an `assertBusy` then we can just assert that there's exactly one task in the response to trigger the needed retries.
Test looks great. I left a few pointers but nothing substantial.

timeline.message:
Tidy up test

- don't wait forever for mount to complete
- document additional required cleanup
- add ESTestCase#safeGet and use it

timeline.body:
Would rather not use abbrs. for var. names wherever poss. :)

Here I think I'd just inline the variable, it's only used in one place - saves having to think up a name at all.
I'd use `assertThat(..., hasSize(1))` here - that should give the same information on failure as what you've got here but without needing a hand-crafted message.
Looks good, just a few tiny style points.
